### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, zod face — RIGHT, narrowing only, refusal loud and named.** `DataDisplaySchema` (and through it `AnyComponentSchema`, `safeValidateSchema`, `StrictAnyComponentSchema` and `objectui validate`) stops accepting a `type: "html"` node. The literal is now claimed by `RetiredHtmlNodeSchema`, a `retiredNodeType('html', …)` arm whose `.check` pushes one `custom` issue at `type` unconditionally and whose message names the two remedies (an `html` / `richtext` FIELD, a `kind: 'html'` page). Nothing refused before is accepted now. The arm is the shape of `RetiredKanbanNodeSchema` (objectui#8802) and the `cloud:plan-status` arm (objectui#12954); it has no TypeScript twin, is exported by its module only, and `@object-ui/types`'s `exports` map reaches `./zod` through `index.zod.ts`, which does not re-export it — so nothing published parses against it. Pinned with a firing control (`kbd` still parses) and a separator control (an unknown literal takes the generic path without the retirement text).
- **Public surface, `@object-ui/types` — RIGHT, nothing dangles.** The `HtmlSchema` interface leaves `data-display.ts`, so BOTH published entries that carried it lose the export: `.` (`index.ts`) and the `./data-display` subpath (the changeset says "from the package entry"; the subpath goes with it and FROM → TO "there is no such export" still covers it). The `SchemaRegistry` row `'html'` leaves, so `ComponentType` narrows (compile-time pins with non-vacuity siblings). The zod `HtmlSchema` leaves `./zod`. Head tree: no importer of `HtmlSchema` remains; `zod-mirror-parity` moves 205 → 204 with the refusal arm in `EXCLUSIONS`, not `MIRRORS`; `arm-named-export-8784` carries an `ABSENT_BY_DECISION` row quoting the barrel's own sentence.
- **Registry — RIGHT.** `html.tsx` is deleted and its `import './html';` line is gone, so neither `ui:html` nor the bare `html` key is registered. `@object-ui/fields` keeps `html` in `FIELD_TYPES_SKIP_FALLBACK`, so the bare key resolves to NOTHING (the OBJUI-001 panel), never to the rich-text editor, and `field:html` stays the widget's only key. Pinned with lit controls (`text` / `ui:text` registered; `field:html` registered) in components, fields and the console graph. No alias, no fallback.
- **Curated tier — RIGHT.** `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` loses `html`, so `getPublicConfigs()`, both console manifest producers and `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` (regenerated by its own generator; `objectui check`) stop naming it. `public-contract`'s `EXPECTED_COVERED` and `html-tier-manifest`'s curated pin read the live manifest, not the roster, so a stray registration would surface.
- **The `kind: 'html'` page tier — RIGHT, a measured second door.** `getJsxManifest()` whitelists `ComponentRegistry.getKnownTypes()`, so at the base an html tag carrying an html attribute compiled with no diagnostic and reached the sink; at the head the parser's `forbidden-tag` and the validator's `unknown-component` refuse it. The console pin drives the real `compile` and `SchemaRenderer` over the full registration graph with a payload (an img element carrying an onerror attribute) and a control page that renders its text. `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md` now says there is no raw-HTML block on either tier.
- **Doc gate — RIGHT, not a tolerance shim.** The `check-doc-component-types.mjs` exemption for `content/docs/fields/rich-text.mdx` names the FIELD literal (`HtmlFieldMetadata`), the gate's designed carrier with a written reason, and the gate's own "no longer matches the tree" leg guards its staleness. Both `type: 'html'` on that page are the field type; the catalog's `fields-rich-text/html-editor` document is the field type and the types test's suite 4 pins that it still validates.
- **Shifted counts — RIGHT, two-way pins kept.** `widget-dom-leak-sweep` 150/82/133/147/168 → 149/81/132/146/167 with `componentsClean` 68 unchanged (149 − 81 = 68); `content-channel-family-d` 67 → 66 rows and 66 × 2 − 3 cases; `NAMESPACED_REFUSED_AT_TYPE` 307 → 306 with `ui:html` named as the one leaver and the bare count unmoved (the bare key was armed, its arm became a refusal).
- **Dangling check — RIGHT.** At the head `HtmlSchema` survives only in the changeset, retirement comments and a dated audit; `ui:html` only in tests and comments; no README and nothing under `skills/**` names the node; the docs page, its `meta.json` row and its index link leave together; the catalog example and its generated index leave together; `data-display-examples.json`'s `html` entry leaves with no reader expecting it. Not governed: the 31 paths hit none of objectui's `GOVERNED_SURFACES` rows.
- **Gate verdicts on this head.** Every check-run is `success` — Repo Gates, Lint, Type Check, Test shards 1..16/16, Test (dist pins), Build & E2E, Build Docs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Line Citation Gate, Changeset Bump Policy / Declaration / Claim Re-read / Fixed Group Check / Overwrite Report, Bundle Analysis, Live E2E; only the path-gated coverage shards and `dependabot` are skipped. No red on the head.

### ② Semver level

- **Level and packages — RIGHT.** `minor` on `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/cli`: exactly the four whose published behaviour moves. `@object-ui/fields` moved a comment and regrouped one Set member with no behaviour change, is not named, and the `fixed` group bumps it regardless. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a node type removed) takes `minor`; no `major`, per this repository's version policy (Changeset Bump Policy green). The body states the breaking semantics, carries FROM → TO for each of the three surfaces (node, public block, schema) and the one-line fix, and separates the untouched `html` FIELD type. The title carries `!`.
- **The declaration line — WRONG on both carriers.** The PR body and the changeset each spell the line as `Clause-②: no` with NO direction arm. The fleet's one reader of that line (`clause2-line.mjs`, `CLAUSE2_ARMS`) documents a bare `no` as declaring NO DIRECTION; the arm exists because a breaking narrowing hidden under a bare `no` is the measured gap the maintainer ruled closed on objectstack#16421 — and this diff is that case exactly: a published accept set and three exports narrowed. The recogniser (`reviewFace`), run over this PR's 31 paths, refuses to read the narrowing face off the committed changeset and says why — the changeset's line decides, and only the `(narrowing)` arm selects the narrowing face; without it the face is `declaration`, whose tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`. So as committed, the PR declares itself owed a default-tier review, and the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review it actually owes stands on the dispatch's hand-mandate alone. The changeset also publishes verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md`, where a published paragraph is never re-addressed. objectui's own precedent for this exact shape — the `cloud:plan-status` retirement (objectui#12954) this PR cites, the `filterableFields` retirement, the `DashboardWidgetSchema['type']` narrowing — all read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md`.
  - Origin, named: the claim (comment 6386906709) spelled the bare `no` while its own prose reads "narrows … (BREAKING, `!` changeset)", and `os-dev.md` binds the dev to copy the claim's two lines into the PR body verbatim and never to invent — so the dev's copy is faithful and the misdeclaration is the claim's.
  - Fix, one token on two carriers plus the claim: the dispatch seat amends the claim's line on the card to `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (the dev may not diverge from the claim on its own), then the PR body's line and the changeset's line take the same spelling. That is a new head; this record is of `bfd3722` only.

3. Attribution — all five branch commits end with the model-free pair (`Claude-Session:` and `Co-authored-by: Claude`); the PR body carries the session-URL footer; a comment carries the bare form, as below. Correct under the precedence both AGENTS.md files state. Accepted.

6. Worktree removed after the PR opened — process. Accepted.
7. Out-of-scope (carrier: objectstack's next `.objectui-sha` bump) — objectstack's repo-root `sdui.manifest.json` still names `html` ("Raw HTML content"): confirmed at objectstack's current tree. `check-sdui-manifest.mjs` check 3 (STALENESS: the record's `objectuiSha` must equal `.objectui-sha`) reds the bump PR until the manifest is regenerated from the new pin, which drops the entry. Until then objectstack's `validateJsxPages` reads that `components` map as its tag set and admits the tag, AND the pinned console build (`.objectui-sha` at `2958f17e…`) still RENDERS the node — the shipped console keeps the sink until the bump. ESCALATED to the PM: the pin bump is the carrier of this p1 fix for objectstack's shipped console and should follow this landing promptly; its manifest regenerate is forced by that gate. Not a defect of this PR.
8.
